statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-49834 (GHSA-9vcr-p3rj-q5q6, GO-2026-5952): in sigstore-go, a verifier configured to require more than one transparency log entry or signed certificate timestamp (WithTransparencyLog or WithSignedCertificateTimestamps with a threshold above 1) counted verified entries per entry or per validation path rather than per log, so a single compromised log could satisfy the multi-log threshold. It affects github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go up to and including 1.1.4 and is fixed in 1.2.0 by commit dbb07e62 (https://github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/commit/dbb07e62623edd5b175fb9dd5a41dcb85a159207, pull request 633), which changes pkg/verify/tlog.go and pkg/verify/sct.go. Sources: https://github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/security/advisories/GHSA-9vcr-p3rj-q5q6, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5952 and https://github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/releases/tag/v1.2.0. We checked every scout-sbom-indexer-dev package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository as of 28 November 2026: 25 builds, 1.20.4-r1 to the current 1.30.0-r0, on x86_64 and aarch64 (50 packages). Each package holds one file, /sbom-indexer, a statically linked Go program for Linux built with CGO_ENABLED=0 (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies). We read the program in full from every package, except 1.26.0-r3, whose program has the same SHA-1 checksum, recorded in its package header, as the 1.26.0-r2 program we read. The -dev program is built without the -w linker flag and without -trimpath; its Go release and module versions are the same as those of the scout-sbom-indexer program of the same build. Its Go build information lists github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go, the same on both architectures and with no replace directive for that module: v1.1.4 in 1.20.4-r1 to 1.23.1-r0, v1.2.0 in 1.23.1-r1, v1.2.1 in 1.23.1-r3 to 1.23.1-r10, v1.2.2 in 1.26.0-r1 to 1.30.0-r0. Reading the program's Go function table in every build (runtime.main found in every build as a control) shows that the only sigstore-go functions linked are the package initializers of pkg/bundle and pkg/verify (bundle.init and verify.init); no other pkg/verify function, including VerifyTlogEntry and VerifySignedCertificateTimestamp, is in the function table of any build. A byte search of every build, which also finds the names of functions the compiler inlined, finds none of VerifyTlogEntry, VerifySignedCertificateTimestamp, WithTransparencyLog and WithSignedCertificateTimestamps; the only sigstore-go/pkg/verify. names are verify..inittask, verify.init and verify.treeIDSuffixRegex, while the same search finds runtime.main in every build. So the sigstore-go verification code this advisory concerns is not present in any build, whichever sigstore-go version the build information names. Debian 13 marks its sigstore-go package no-dsa for this CVE (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-49834); this decision rests on the code in these builds, not on that status.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-49834 (GHSA-9vcr-p3rj-q5q6, GO-2026-5952): in sigstore-go, a verifier configured to require more than one transparency log entry or signed certificate timestamp (WithTransparencyLog or WithSignedCertificateTimestamps with a threshold above 1) counted verified entries per entry or per validation path rather than per log, so a single compromised log could satisfy the multi-log threshold. It affects github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go up to and including 1.1.4 and is fixed in 1.2.0 by commit dbb07e62 (https://github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/commit/dbb07e62623edd5b175fb9dd5a41dcb85a159207, pull request 633), which changes pkg/verify/tlog.go and pkg/verify/sct.go. Sources: https://github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/security/advisories/GHSA-9vcr-p3rj-q5q6, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5952 and https://github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go/releases/tag/v1.2.0. We checked every scout-sbom-indexer-dev package published for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository as of 28 November 2026: 25 builds, 1.20.4-1 to the current 1.30.0-0, on amd64 and arm64 (50 packages). Each package installs one file, /sbom-indexer, as listed in the md5sums manifest of its control archive, and the MD5 checksum recorded there equals that of the program we read in full from the Alpine 3.23 package of the same version and architecture with the matching revision (for example 1.20.4-5 matches 1.20.4-r5 and 1.21.0-0 matches 1.21.0-r0; 1.26.0-3 matches the 1.26.0-r2 program, which 1.26.0-r3 also carries), so these packages carry the same statically linked Go programs, built with CGO_ENABLED=0 (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies). The -dev program is built without the -w linker flag and without -trimpath; its Go release and module versions are the same as those of the scout-sbom-indexer program of the same build. Its Go build information lists github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go, the same on both architectures and with no replace directive for that module: v1.1.4 in 1.20.4-1 to 1.23.1-0, v1.2.0 in 1.23.1-1, v1.2.1 in 1.23.1-3 to 1.23.1-10, v1.2.2 in 1.26.0-1 to 1.30.0-0. Reading the program's Go function table in every build (runtime.main found in every build as a control) shows that the only sigstore-go functions linked are the package initializers of pkg/bundle and pkg/verify (bundle.init and verify.init); no other pkg/verify function, including VerifyTlogEntry and VerifySignedCertificateTimestamp, is in the function table of any build. A byte search of every build, which also finds the names of functions the compiler inlined, finds none of VerifyTlogEntry, VerifySignedCertificateTimestamp, WithTransparencyLog and WithSignedCertificateTimestamps; the only sigstore-go/pkg/verify. names are verify..inittask, verify.init and verify.treeIDSuffixRegex, while the same search finds runtime.main in every build. So the sigstore-go verification code this advisory concerns is not present in any build, whichever sigstore-go version the build information names. Debian 13 marks its sigstore-go package no-dsa for this CVE (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-49834); this decision rests on the code in these builds, not on that status.
